title: Opposite river point changes offset in combined chloride shares in USGS load estimates for 1980-1996 and 2009-2025
abstract: We tested whether similar combined chloride shares conceal different river changes. We used USGS version 3.0 load estimates at the Mississippi and Atchafalaya outlets. From 1980-1996 to 2009-2025, stationary flow-normalized chloride shares rose from 8.851% to 9.190% at the Mississippi site and fell from 12.219% to 10.700% at the Atchafalaya site. Their combined share fell from 9.854% to 9.625%. Exact accounting gives ratio terms of +0.240 and -0.445 percentage points and a load mix term of -0.024 points. The opposite river point changes persist across three load methods and four late periods. However, adverse ranges from the source annual marginal limits permit either sign for each change. Joint model error is unavailable. These are descriptive model estimates, not resolved trends or evidence of a salt source. The package includes source data, provenance, code, tables, a figure and an independent arithmetic audit.

display.caption: Stationary normalized chloride shares and exact contributions to the combined period change. Point estimates only; source uncertainty permits either sign for the changes.
